Let me break this down step by step. First, I need to understand the situation. I used to be really into working out and had a slim body. But after moving to a new city, I felt lonely and started eating a lot as a coping mechanism. I gained about 10 kilos in six months, which I feel guilty about. My family, including my sister's husband, has noticed the weight gain and the acne from eating unhealthy food. My sister's husband keeps asking me how much I weigh, why I don't go to the gym, and why I eat so much. He does this in an arrogant way, probably because he's a bodybuilder with a clean diet. I can tell he's trying to make me feel bad, and it's really affecting me. I feel guilty and tired, and I'm struggling to motivate myself to go back to the gym or even do my chores. Now, I'm considering whether I should tell him he's a jerk and to stop his comments. I know that fat acceptance isn't the solution, and I shouldn't encourage myself to tolerate a harmful lifestyle. But his comments are really getting to me. I think about why he's doing this. Maybe he's trying to help, but his approach is wrong. Or maybe he's insecure about something else and taking it out on me. Either way, his comments are hurtful and not constructive. I also consider how telling him off might affect our relationship. If I confront him, could it lead to more tension or even a breakdown in our relationship? On the other hand, if I don't say anything, I might continue to feel hurt and demoralized, which isn't good for my mental health. I wonder if there's a better way to address his comments without being confrontational. Maybe I could talk to him calmly about how his words affect me and ask him to stop. But I'm not sure if he'd listen or if he'd take it the right way. Another angle is to think about whether his comments are actually helpful. If he's trying to encourage me to lose weight, his approach is counterproductive. Instead of motivating me, he's making me feel worse about myself. So, his behavior is not only unkind but also ineffective. I also think about my own feelings. I'm already struggling with guilt and low energy. Dealing with his comments adds to that stress. It's important for me to have a supportive environment, especially when I'm trying to make changes in my life. Maybe I should also consider talking to my sister about this, as she might be able to mediate or support me. But I don't want to cause any issues between her and her husband if possible. In the end, I have to decide whether confronting him is the right move. It might help me feel empowered and set boundaries, but it could also lead to conflict. Alternatively, I could focus on my own journey and try to ignore his comments, but that might not be healthy either. I think the key points are: his comments are hurtful and unconstructive, they're affecting my mental health, and I have the right to set boundaries. So, maybe it's worth telling him how his words make me feel, even if it's difficult.
